relevance_note: Family case report of seven relatives carrying a heterozygous TNFAIP3 c.2209delC mutation: 'P1–P7 were all diagnosed with HA20'.
method_note: Built by hand with a small Python script (no table transcription; Tables 1 and 2 have only captions in the Markdown, no contents, so thyroid test values, antibody levels and HLA types are not available). Labels P1–P7 are the paper's own. Variant fields come from the Discussion sentence naming the group 'the present family (P1–P7)' and 'a heterozygous c.2209delC mutation that was present in all members tested'; transcript NM_006290.2 is printed for the family's variant; the abstract calls it 'novel' while the Discussion says its in vitro functional analysis was previously reported (2) - pathogenicity recorded as 'pathogenic mutation' only. Inheritance: P1 recorded 'inherited maternal' because P2 is stated to be P1's mother and P2 is among P1–P7 who carry the variant; for P2 (P3 is P1's maternal grandmother, not called P2's mother), P7 (P1's sister; P2 not called her mother) and others inheritance left 'not reported'; no de novo statement. Variant type not stated (no 'frameshift'), so 'not reported'. Ethnicity 'Japanese' is from the statement that this family was described in a study of 'nine independent Japanese families'. Hedged findings recorded with the paper's hedge in the feature text ('possible Crohn’s disease' for P2; P7's perineal fistula 'possibly associated with inflammatory bowel disease'); the gastrointestinal checklist item is left 'not reported' for P1, P2 and P7 because no inflammation/ulcer is stated definitively (P1 bloody stools only). P1, P6 and P7: 'normal thyroid functions and no anti-thyroid autoantibodies' recorded as excluded features, but checklist 'autoimmune thyroiditis' left 'not reported' because the authors add they 'are too young for this to be apparent', and 'autoantibodies (ANA/other)' left 'not reported' (only anti-thyroid antibodies addressed). Stomatitis (P3, P4) is not mapped to checklist 'oral ulcers' (ulcers not stated). P4's Hodgkin lymphoma and craniopharyngioma are recorded as features but not mapped to 'lymphoproliferation' or 'CNS involvement'. P2's cervical lymphadenitis is mapped to 'lymphoproliferation or lymphadenopathy'; P2's chronic mild hepatitis is not called autoimmune, so 'autoimmune hepatitis' is not reported. HT diagnosis ages (P2 28 yr, P3 27 yr) are recorded as feature onsets, not as age at diagnosis (the age at HA20 diagnosis is not given). Ages at P4's (34 yr) and P5's (9 yr) antibody tests are not recorded as last evaluation. P6 onset 'before the age of 1 yr' given no ISO value (upper bound only). The statement 'P2–P6 also experienced some episodes suggestive of an autoinflammatory disease' was not recorded as a feature. No contradictions found.
